SharedFlowBundle.name: ISAM-JWT-SAML
SharedFlowBundle.Description:
Type 5: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) style request to ISAM's JWT-SAML endpoint -- application/x-www-form-urlencoded, NOT a plain JSON body. The subject_token form field holds a JSON *string*; subject_token_type, grant_type, requested_token_type and audience are sibling form fields. The response is still JSON with a SAML assertion embedded (assumed field "saml"; not a confirmed ISAM contract, see the top-level README). Calls the shared ISAM-Common-* building blocks for the actual ISAM callout, signature validation, compression, and header-setting, same as every other type.
Two request variants, chosen by which identity the caller presented (see JS-Build-TokenExchange-Request / resources/jsc/build-token- exchange-request.js for the exact shapes): - Authorization: Bearer token + client certificate -> principal is the fixed "TECHNICAL-USER"; subject_token_type is isam.config.subjectTokenTypeAccessToken; the token and the certificate/DN go in a contextAttributes block. - X-User-Id header, no bearer token -> principal is that user ID; subject_token_type is isam.config.subjectTokenTypeUserId; no contextAttributes at all. Exactly one of the two must be present (RF-Missing-Subject-Identity otherwise); if both are somehow present, the bearer-token variant wins.
